recipes.name: Mediterranean Lamb and Lentil Stew
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds lamb shoulder arm chops, cubed, round bones reserved
1 cup lentils, picked over and rinsed
2 cups chicken broth, or more as needed

steps.text: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add lamb cubes and bones and brown on all sides, about 3 minutes. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Add onion and garlic and continue cooking about 2 minutes, stirring frequently.

Stir in lentils, 2 cups of chicken broth, tomatoes, carrots and thyme, sage and basil. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the lentils are tender but not quite done, stirring occasionally. Depending on the type and freshness of the lentils, this will take from 15 to 30 minutes. If the stew seems dry, add more broth (up to one cup additional). Discard the lamb bones.
Add spinach and cook 5 minutes more. Stir in lemon zest and juice. Garnish individual servings with some crumbled cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Mediterranean Lamb and Lentil Stew
raw_recipe.description: This lamb and lentil stew is finished with lemon then served with crumbled ricotta salata or feta cheese for a perfect springtime meal. Serve with rice or, ideally, a pilaf.

review.reviewBody: I hate to be one of those people who changes the recipe and then reviews it, but alas, my nature can't help fiddling... when I think lamb and lentils, I think Middle Eastern, so I switched up the spices a bit, but this is a great recipe nonetheless and one I will certainly make again and again! Changes I made were: 1) used lamb loin chops instead of shoulder arm because that's all I could find 2) altered spices to about 1/4 tsp each of fresh rosemary and thyme, plus 1/2 tsp each of freshly-ground coriander and cumin, a pinch or 2 of garam masala, a pinch of powdered ginger, and lots of freshly-ground black pepper 3) cut the lemon to half, because after tasting found that was plenty (and I'm a lemon fanatic) 4) used crushed tomatoes instead of diced because I have an anti-tomato-chunk person in the family 5) added about 1/4 cup red wine and 6) cooked in a slow cooker after browning lamb and cooking onion and garlic. Don't mean to insult the creator at all, because I'm sure it's fantastic the original way, and it was fantastic with a couple alterations! Seriously yummy!

Great soup/stew! My husband took some lamb off a shoulder, to make a lamb roast (stuffed with goat cheese, raisins, garlic, herbs), and I said save me the done with a title meat on it for lentil soup. So I made this soup without the pound of lamb, just the bones with a little meat attached. I also kept the stock (juices) from the roast and threw that into the soup pot. I was worried about the cheese and lemon, however, those are added at the end; so we tried it without them and with them. Those two ingredients, esp. the lemon, took it over the top. I had Meyer lemons, and by adding lemon juice to each bowl before serving the lemon really brightened the soup, and made it shine! I don’t know how else to describe it. I substituted feta for the salata ricotta, because that’s what I had on hand. Once again the cheese really did add to the flavor. I served it with crusty bread, great dipped into the soup for a few bites here and there-delicious! I diced the carrots, and liked that they were similar in size to the lentils both when eating and in appearance.

Awesome! First time I've ever made lamb stew too. I used pre-chopped lamb cubes instead. My only tweaks were to season the lamb before browning. Once done, transfer to a crock pot. Cook onion and garlic in those juices, then add the rest as per the recipe. I only let it simmer covered on stovetop for 10 minutes, then transferred everything to the crock pot for two hours. Stellar! (My other thing was I cooked some lamb several days prior, so I created a cups worth of stock from the bones with some onion, and spices. I think it gave more body to the flavour.)

Great in the slow cooker! I had a leftover bone with meat on it and put that, plus all the ingredients in the slow cooker on High for 6 hours. It did need an extra cup of liquid. Only used half a lemon as others suggested. Super easy perfection!

Nice recipe. I did a few tweaks. I used 2 lamb shanks, seasoned with salt, pepper, dried oregano, thyme, and garlic powder. (They weighed about a pound each with the bones.) I browned them and added some port sherry and chicken broth and simmered them with fresh rosemary & thyme sprigs for about an hour. I strained the broth then sauteed the veg. I added celery because I had some and like it. I followed the recipe after that, except that I used fresh, chopped rosemary and thyme. I also used rotel tomatoes for a little heat. I have never used the ricotta salata before. I found it at Whole Foods. It was nice in this dish, but not sure what else to do with it.

Awesome. First time cooking lamb in a stew and this was the bomb. I omitted the chicken broth and lemon altogether because there was already too much liquid. I did add one beef bouillon cube and simmered it uncovered to reduce the liquid. Also added rosemary. Great over brown rice.

I made this dish tonight and it was delicious. Perfect for a cold winter night and a spouse with a cold. I used homemade lamb stock (it was really, really good stock that I would not waste on a mediocre dish), two carrots plus one parsnip, and otherwise followed the recipe as stated (I cooked it for longer to ensure the lentils were cooked). Thanks for sharing.

Love this recipe!! I made it without the sage and cheese, and it was still delicious! I didn't have fresh spinach, but I used frozen spinach--I just cooked it and put it in at the very end. Lamb on the bone is the best to use since it brings out so much flavor. I had to cook the stew a bit longer than what the recipe called for so that the lentils and carrots were fully cooked. I just kept my eye on it, and it was okay. We are a fan of using cilantro with any lamb dish, so I garnished the stew with fresh cilantro right before serving it. My husband nearly licked the bowl, so I know I will be making this recipe again!

Excellent flavor but we added canned Fire Roasted Tomatoes and ONLY used Fresh Herbs- also the lamb was left over from Rotisserie and cubed- and added for the last 10 minutes of cooking. Did not use the ricotta cheese and only used a PINCH of lemon zest. (We tested a small bite with more lemon and felt it overtook the dish). Otherwise a simple dish and very hearty and filling. Would recommend serving with fresh baked pita bread and sliced cucumber. LOVED this dish!!

Wow, this is fantastic! Thank you for posting. I had leftover lamb roast from Easter and read many reviews here. I chopped the lamb (boneless) and added it toward the end (it softened up nicely). I used a can of fire roasted diced tomatoes. Spices - as listed, added rosemary. This is one of those great recipes that you can spice it up however you like. I'm sticking to the recipe and also rosemary. If you like lemon and fresh baby spinach (like we do) don't forget to add it near the end! Also loved crumbled feta on top in each bowl. We ate it just as it is, but tomorrow's leftovers will be over rice or potatoes or pasta, who knows. This is a keeper.

Amazing recipe. Taste is incredible! I used lamb neck fillet found in the reduced section and it came out so tender. Also used yellow and green split peas instead of lentils, was gorgeous! Thanks for the recipe :)
I added cubed sweet potato because I had one. Delicious

I used leftover lamb, and skipped the chickpeas, adding 1/4 tsp Harissa spice, as well as some frozen kale for green vegetables. Outstanding! I would make it with the chickpeas for vegetarians and with the lamb for meat eaters. I would be very easy to make it all the way to the last, then split into two pots, one with chickpeas and one with lamb for a dinner party for everyone.
light and delicious

This recipe is delicious very flavorful. The only thing I did different was use fresh sage because I had it on hand. I did taste it prior to adding the lemon and next time I would omit the lemon just my opinion. I will definitely make it again.
Rich and filling; my rank of four is solely because the flavor was a little bland. Both my wife, and our nephew who lives with us, voiced approval, Rafael in the best way, by eating two big servings.
Delicious! And I'm not crazy about lamb. All the ingredients blend wonderfully and make the lamb flavor more subtle.
Loved this dish. A crowd favorite. Don't skip the ricotta salata.

This stew was so good that I would eat two bowls per meal. I substituted ground lamb for the chops, added finely chopped red potatoes, and substituted fresh turnip greens from my garden for the spinach.

Great recipe! Made it with lamb chops, so couldn’t really get rid of bones, but it didn’t ruin it at all. Came out great! Also, not a big fan of lemon, so didn’t use it. Instead, I added 4 mini Bella mushrooms, finely chopped - anyways, thanks for great recipe!
